native_progress_main.synthesis:
STATE OF KNOWLEDGE — 2026-09-08, continuation audit + incremental primary-source literature review.

Scope: pre-rendered audio -> stage lighting; whole-song context allowed; dance is training supervision only. The old causal-only/no-experiments synthesis is superseded. Current learned renderer uses the descriptor/event/style model with ConductorHybrid. Stage9 GroupEngine and generic CLI are separate entry points.

Local evidence: repeated tuning of stems, frozen audio features, model size, per-bar level regression, six-moment group decoding and critic/cue recipes did not close the designed-appearance gap. Strong synchronization scores can coexist with poor aesthetics. Historical supports/directional-only records are not blanket product gates. GroupDecoder is not a faithful Skip-BART/SeqLight implementation: it omits autoregressive light tokens, histogram targets and learned temporal decomposition. Existing recurrence analysis retains boundaries but not motif memory. Per-bar regression therefore does not rule out explicit motif reuse.

Human pilot:39ratings, one rater,29registered song groups. Held-out preference-model accuracy56.4%/59.0% with intervals including chance; music accuracy equals its majority-side baseline and appearance logloss0.739 is worse than0.693 chance. Fresh generated-candidate-vs-default wins are unmeasured. These ratings do not test new GroupEngine wave/colour controls. Median screen-luma mismatch16.1%; the blinder metric squares dimmer while the renderer is linear. Preserve old data/scores, version the correction, verify canonical audio identity and material matching before fresh preference claims.

New literature adds implementable SLS/EUBO preference acquisition, editable light-object layers (Glow with the Flow), explicit hierarchical/repetition representations, Beat This timing models and Raveform annotation access. Transfer to LightSem is untested. Glow with the Flow itself reports that synchronization/congruence ratings miss repetition and colour-richness defects. SeqLight weight release is not verified. RPMC is video-derived colour supervision, not professional DMX logs; no newly usable authored-control corpus was established.

Next experiments, in order of dependencies: material/metric validation; isolated beat benchmark; explicit recurrence-memory vs equally varied no-memory composition; active vs random pair acquisition; histogram/assignment oracle followed only conditionally by matched audio-conditioned training; independently reviewed authored-look oracle to measure renderer/planner capability. Budgets and thresholds in the report are proposals, not preregistrations. Confirm primary outcomes, independence unit and gates before execution; do not interpret an oracle failure as a uniquely identified cause.

No new training/rendering/GPU job or experiment closure was performed in this review. Additional Just Dance extraction remains a separate process; freeze and audit completed features before using new data. Existing interpretation debt and statuses are not cleared by this synthesis. Sources and detailed report: /root/lightsem/docs/research/2026-09-08/LightSem_Research_Review_2026-09-08.pdf; local evidence /root/lightsem/docs/CONTINUATION_AUDIT_2026-09-07.md and /root/lightsem/docs/HL_RATINGS_2026-09-08.md.

native_problem.title: Sound -> light for concerts/festivals, TRAINED ON DANCE datasets (LightSem v2): generative audio -> light on dance-derived targets
native_problem.description: Accepted representation-first implementation 2026-09-10. Build convincing music-driven stage lighting. Music is the only playback input; an internal generated skeleton/motion sequence is explicitly allowed. Hybrid measured audio dynamics may control brightness and movement intensity. Quiet passages must remain visible but restrained. Establish clean motion-source and temporal-codec quality before audio training. Prior human review rejects flashing/juggling reconstructions and excessive Shpongle movement; only the incumbent audio-to-descriptions-to-pose path is currently visually convincing. Glare improvement is useful but does not establish visible head-brightness dynamics. Exploration seed0; confirm only qualifying finalist and matched baseline at seed1. Accelerated BF16/compile/prefetch in matched arms, no earlier 2–3h ceiling. Historical nulls and gates remain valid.

updates.text: 2026-09-03 rev. 2 (Anton's correction): dance datasets are the TRAINING SET for a sound->light model; no music-to-dance generation at inference. Rev. 1's 'latent dancer' inference path is withdrawn; generators survive only as an optional offline pseudo-labelling teacher (PLAN.md section 8). Runbooks rb-ls2-00..05 rewritten accordingly.

2026-09-04 rev. 3: integrated four Perplexity reasoning passes (audio->light design; music-induced-movement science; causal model + latency; dataset audit degenerated, replaced by direct source checks) and Anton's note on extracting motion from video with pose models. Targets split into deterministic skeleton / event point-process / sampled style residual; rig mapping follows the body; two-path deployment (transients on a 10-20 ms DSP path) because ITU-R BT.1359-1 detectability is +45 ms when sound leads. New runbooks 00b (predictability audit) and 00c (late-lights + category-error tests) run BEFORE any training.

2026-09-04 Stage 0b resolved in two halves (exp-002, exp-003). AIST++ cannot supply block A: genre explains 0.65-0.96 of between-track movement variance and Burger 2013 does not replicate, several correlations invert. Free dancing to EDM can: held-out-track R2 +0.30 for the shared movement curve on Oslo, drop/breakdown ratio 1.7-2.5x with Cohen's d up to 2.55. The binding constraint moves from 'is there a signal' to 'how much free-dance data can we get'.

2026-09-04 implementation pass complete (exp-004..exp-008): descriptor extractor (mocap and video), constant-tempo beat grid, canonical-rig conductors, evaluation suite with nulls, 9.3 M causal Conformer with three heads, streaming inference, blind A/B harness; 14 of 14 verification checks. Stage 1 light gates fail (+0.017 vs real-mapped +0.216); operator head passes (+0.31 lift, z 3.66); latency budget met.

2026-09-04 repair pass (exp-009): the Stage 1 audio bus read up to 375 ms of the future through librosa defaults; fixed, retrained, held-out block A R2 +0.0438 -> +0.0192, which is the size of the artefact. Event-rate calibration did not raise Light-BAS (predicted mechanism wrong). The surplus light events come from the sampled channels' 11-452x corpus HF energy. Product pivoted to the offline pre-rendered path (rb-ls2-07, PLAN rev. 6).

2026-09-04 Stage 0c category test (exp-010): dance-derived hybrid light beats the beat trigger 8-1 (1 equal) on 'looks like a lighting engineer', ties 5-4 on 'on the music'; one rater, 10 brightness-matched AIST++ pairs. Category error rejected directionally; block C stays. Rater's tell for 'not an engineer' was change rate, the same defect the model carries.

2026-09-04 Stage 8 queued (rb-ls2-08): 338 Just Dance gameplay captures (22.0 h, full songs, one filmed stylised coach or several -- each coach its own channel; research-only). Three signals: coach motion for block A/C, hand-animated background lighting as a designed show for HEAD B, full-song structure for H-C. Decision measurement is the held-out-song predictability audit. Extraction launched 15:00 with YOLO26m-pose at 960 after a six-clip trial (solos and multi-coach at >= 0.998 coverage per coach).

2026-09-04 Stage 7 (rb-ls2-07), three of four hypotheses tested. H-A (exp-012): the look-ahead ceiling fails both gates -- with the whole track visible, held-out block A R2 on AIST++ is -0.009 against the causal +0.019 and the light gates do not move; the corpus binds, not the model. H-B (exp-011): spectral matching is the largest lever found -- a causal one-pole per channel fitted to the corpus above-6 Hz energy takes model Light-BAS from +0.018 to +0.293 (real-mapped +0.211), FID 67 -> 20, light events 86 -> 35 per clip against 30 real, diversity not falling; the 12 Hz filter the hypothesis named does nothing, the mismatch sits near 0.2 Hz; zero-phase at matched cutoffs scores the same, so the offline path removes lag, not jitter. H-D (exp-013): audio alone does not anticipate an operator's scene change 4 s ahead (offline margin -0.02, CI spanning zero); a 10x first result was a leak through target-derived hazard features under a symmetric window, caught by the shift control. H-C waits for the Just Dance corpus.

2026-09-04 (evening) Stage 9 queued (rb-ls2-09-designed-light, PLAN.md rev. 8 section 6.9). Anton's reading of the shipped Just Dance model: decent, not human. Five outside passes with the full brief (Perplexity deep research x1, reasoning x4: audio decomposition, datasets in two halves, multimodal methods, mixture of light) plus Skip-BART (arXiv:2506.01482) and SeqLight (arXiv:2605.03660) read in full agree on the diagnosis: the bottleneck is the target (dance is a weak proxy; coaches agree at r 0.22-0.42), the hand-written conductor, and the absence of human preference -- not the trunk, causality or the amount of dance. Deep-research verdict: 'another music-to-motion transformer will not close the gap; the project needs authored lighting intent, a learned hierarchical planner, and a preference model that tells deliberate composition from synchronised motion'. Datasets: no public, commercially clean corpus of professional DMX programming exists; RPMC-L2 (all 699 now cached, CC-BY-4.0, no waveform) is the only public stage-domain set; authored light exists at scale in xLights free .xsq sequences (~556, ~25-40 h, audio not included) and Beat Saber lightshow maps (v3 group event boxes with phase-spread filters, verified on the API); console show files only by contract. Seven hypotheses queued: H-G stems (audit-gated), H-H corpus predictability gate, H-I group-effects decoder (the mixture of light, SeqLight's split), H-J section planner on the knobs, H-K factorised critic with beat-trigger negatives as best-of-N, H-L Bradley-Terry knobs from 200-400 pairs, H-M frozen encoder vs random projection. Rule-outs added: AR light LM decoder, RL on the flow head before the critic gate, type-MoE in the trunk, section/chord/LRA/timbre bus channels, Jukebox/CLAP, fixture-token decoder before console data, product training on research corpora.

2026-09-05: Stage 9 (rb-ls2-09) run end to end; H-H, H-G, H-M, H-J, H-K directional-only, H-I refuted as built, H-L open (exp-017..023). Reading: the authored corpora on disk (RPMC-L2, Just Dance visual, Beat Saber) support learning WHEN a look changes and the corpus's look statistics, not per-frame or per-bar light levels; the decent-not-human gap is not closed by stems, a frozen encoder, a regressed or sampled group decoder, a bar planner or a critic reranker. Engine diagnostic: with the phase spread zeroed the v1 decoder's Light-BAS minus null is +0.51 (conductor +0.13) at fewer events than the conductor, so the BAS miss was the engine; FID_light and the missing human test carry the verdict. Next: cue-based rendering from the calibrated look-change hazard, scored on cue timing and look-transition statistics; the H-L human preference study; console show files for level design.

2026-09-10 explicit user authorization: implement the accepted representation-first plan. This supersedes prior no-internal-motion restrictions. Previous description preserved:
Binding product objective, clarified by Anton on2026-09-08: lights and moving fixtures should dance to music using a model trained on measured dancer motion. Inference takes music only; no dancer or pose input is required. Whole-song context is allowed. No algorithmic beat/downbeat/bar grid, BPM metronome, preset pulse/chase/strobe, travelling wave, sinusoidal aiming or hue-drift generator may supply the choreography. Fixture translation may convert learned controls into geometry/DMX and enforce physical ranges/speed limits without inventing temporal patterns. With fixed learned controls, light should settle to a fixed state.

The current Stage11 scene path does not meet this objective. It predicts six scene-colour statistics and then applies fixed beat pulses/waves. The Shpongle demonstration used a90BPM uniform grid (0.666667s intervals); Anton observed repetitive flashing. The separate learned-descriptor aiming prototype removed the pan/tilt pendulum only. The historical motion model also includes beat-derived input features and a music-relative metric_level target; masking inputs only at inference would not constitute a validated beat-free trained model.

Stage11's limited positive findings remain: temporal scene dynamics and audio-conditioning controls passed independently audited validation and locked-test gates (H11-T/A supports), but expanded-data motion improvement failed validation (H11-D directional_only). This is not an end-to-end aesthetic or dance-transfer win. The39-rating H-L pilot remains unconfirmed and new48-pair materials are unrated. Historical Stage9/10 recipe failures and their scope remain preserved. The immediate architecture requirement and limitations are recorded in /root/lightsem/docs/DANCE_DRIVEN_CONTRACT.md and /root/lightsem/docs/STAGE11_RESULTS_20260908.md. native_problem.synthesis:
STATE OF KNOWLEDGE — 2026-09-08, continuation audit + incremental primary-source literature review.

Scope: pre-rendered audio -> stage lighting; whole-song context allowed; dance is training supervision only. The old causal-only/no-experiments synthesis is superseded. Current learned renderer uses the descriptor/event/style model with ConductorHybrid. Stage9 GroupEngine and generic CLI are separate entry points.

Local evidence: repeated tuning of stems, frozen audio features, model size, per-bar level regression, six-moment group decoding and critic/cue recipes did not close the designed-appearance gap. Strong synchronization scores can coexist with poor aesthetics. Historical supports/directional-only records are not blanket product gates. GroupDecoder is not a faithful Skip-BART/SeqLight implementation: it omits autoregressive light tokens, histogram targets and learned temporal decomposition. Existing recurrence analysis retains boundaries but not motif memory. Per-bar regression therefore does not rule out explicit motif reuse.

Human pilot:39ratings, one rater,29registered song groups. Held-out preference-model accuracy56.4%/59.0% with intervals including chance; music accuracy equals its majority-side baseline and appearance logloss0.739 is worse than0.693 chance. Fresh generated-candidate-vs-default wins are unmeasured. These ratings do not test new GroupEngine wave/colour controls. Median screen-luma mismatch16.1%; the blinder metric squares dimmer while the renderer is linear. Preserve old data/scores, version the correction, verify canonical audio identity and material matching before fresh preference claims.

New literature adds implementable SLS/EUBO preference acquisition, editable light-object layers (Glow with the Flow), explicit hierarchical/repetition representations, Beat This timing models and Raveform annotation access. Transfer to LightSem is untested. Glow with the Flow itself reports that synchronization/congruence ratings miss repetition and colour-richness defects. SeqLight weight release is not verified. RPMC is video-derived colour supervision, not professional DMX logs; no newly usable authored-control corpus was established.

Next experiments, in order of dependencies: material/metric validation; isolated beat benchmark; explicit recurrence-memory vs equally varied no-memory composition; active vs random pair acquisition; histogram/assignment oracle followed only conditionally by matched audio-conditioned training; independently reviewed authored-look oracle to measure renderer/planner capability. Budgets and thresholds in the report are proposals, not preregistrations. Confirm primary outcomes, independence unit and gates before execution; do not interpret an oracle failure as a uniquely identified cause.

No new training/rendering/GPU job or experiment closure was performed in this review. Additional Just Dance extraction remains a separate process; freeze and audit completed features before using new data. Existing interpretation debt and statuses are not cleared by this synthesis. Sources and detailed report: /root/lightsem/docs/research/2026-09-08/LightSem_Research_Review_2026-09-08.pdf; local evidence /root/lightsem/docs/CONTINUATION_AUDIT_2026-09-07.md and /root/lightsem/docs/HL_RATINGS_2026-09-08.md.

## Statement
A causal Conformer trained on the product's own causal features beats both the rhythm-of-past-changes baseline and the ridge probe at predicting when a lighting operator changes the scene, and is therefore worth deploying as HEAD B.

## Rationale
Stage 2's probe established the signal on the corpus's openl3 embeddings. openl3 is a 1 s-window embedding and is not the product's conditioning, so the deployable head has to be retrained on causal log-mel, banded flux, onset and beat phase computed the same way the live path computes them.

## Plan
Recompute the product's causal features for all 699 shows from the corpus's own mel spectrogram (52 channels: banded flux and energy, onset, centroid, flatness, rolloff at three causal EMA scales, plus beat phase from a comb grid fitted on kick-band flux). 3.6 M-parameter causal Conformer, 4 blocks, 30 s windows at 10 Hz, BCE hazard. Split by song hash. Baselines fitted on training songs only: rhythm alone, and ridge on the same causal features.

hypotheses.body:
## Statement
A factorised audio-light critic trained with time-shift, other-song AND beat-trigger negatives on bar-synchronous tokens learns something beyond beat and loudness: it separates real authored light from beat-trigger light on held-out songs above chance, its best-of-8 ranking over rectified-flow samples changes when the critic is projected to its nearest additive model, and best-of-8 beats random-of-8 on human 'fits the music'. Without the beat-trigger negative it collapses to a beat detector and rewards the mode the model already occupies.

## Rationale
Contrastive alignment provably captures shared information only (MAS.S60 lecture 06, FactorCL); on this data that is beat + RMS, which is already the model's failure mode (BAS +0.135 vs coach +0.087). A two-head critic (redundant C_R, unique C_U) ranked by C_U - lambda C_R, with the additive-projection test from lecture 07, is the reranker form of FactorCL. Best-of-N through the conductor costs N tiny forward passes; reward use waits for the gate.

## Plan
rb-ls2-09 step 9.5. Dual encoder on bar tokens (audio = 92-ch bus; light = HSV histogram + look-change flag + strobe density); positives RPMC-L2, JD visual, G9.2 corpora; three negative families; instrument: real-vs-shift and real-vs-beat-trigger accuracy, correlation of C with RMS vs with look-change flags, additive projection; best-of-8 over block C samples scored through the conductor; human pairs best-of-8 vs random-of-8 on held-out songs; RPMC-L2 and JD reported separately.

hypotheses.body:
## Statement
A learned group-effects decoder (Anton's mixture of light: a shared type-masked head on the frozen trunk and operator head emitting per-group intensity envelope, palette, effect id, rate in beats, phase spread and density, expanded to DMX by a deterministic effects engine) trained on authored light through a differentiable histogram renderer with random-rig dropout beats the hand-written conductor on Value- and onset-matched held-out songs: FID vs conductor beats a shuffled-donor control by > 2x, BAS is not lower without more onsets, raters prefer it on 'fits the music' with a CI excluding 50% at n >= 20, and it transfers to an unseen patch better than channel-copy.

## Rationale
The conductor owns every artistic decision and the model only steers 30 channels that audio does not predict (block A R2 -0.22). Of the three mixture-of-light architectures, group effects + engine is how shows are programmed, is permutation- and mirror-safe by construction, and is the only one trainable from corpora without per-fixture DMX; SeqLight (arXiv:2605.03660) makes the same split (global HSV distribution, then venue-specific decomposition) and wins its human study 4.54 vs 3.90 vs 2.70. Type is an output mask, not an expert (MAS.S60: partitioned experts under-share).

## Plan
rb-ls2-09 step 9.3. Freeze Conformer + operator head; 0.5-2 M causal head -> group-effect vector at 40 fps; reuse the expander with fixtures sorted by (type, x) and the fitted one-pole; torch histogram renderer (additive coloured blobs; spots as 2-D Gaussians); targets RPMC-L2 + JD visual (+ G9.2 corpora); per-type losses (wash: hue+value histogram, never absolute level; strobe: onset times and duty cycle); aux look-change CE; random-rig dropout; no conductor-DMX distillation; no pan/tilt learning. Eval on held-out songs with Value matched and onset density capped; split FID (hue / onset / full); shuffled-donor control; brightness-matched A/B with a 'too metronomic' question; rig-transfer test; causal and offline.

hypotheses.body:
## Statement
Audio predicts lighting EVENTS (when the scene changes) even though it does not predict lighting LEVELS. Reformulating the target from the absolute scene vector to a change/onset train removes persistence's structural advantage and asks the question a lighting desk actually answers: fire a cue now, or not.

## Rationale
The level-regression refutation showed persistence explains R2_within +0.708 with no audio at all, and audio's marginal was -0.005. But that comparison is rigged by construction: a slowly-varying target is trivially predicted by its own past, and persistence is useless at exactly the moments an operator acts. An event target makes the two competitors meet where neither has a structural edge. multimodal-ai lecture 06 names this failure directly: continuous streams have no natural elements, and treating fixed frames as semantic units is a silent correctness bug -- segment first, then align.

## Plan
Events: per-song z-scored 6-dim light vector, novelty = ||future 1.0s mean - past 1.0s mean||, peaks above the 90th percentile with 2.0s minimum separation. Target: is there an event in the next 1.0s. COMPETITOR is NOT persistence (it cannot predict change) but the RHYTHM of past changes: time since last event, 30s event rate, phase against the song's own median inter-event interval -- a desk firing every N seconds is a real deployable baseline needing no audio. Audio: causal multi-scale past pooling (0.5-4.0s) plus differences between recent and older pools. Metric: per-song AP / base rate, 5-fold CV by song over all 140 songs. Null: 40 reps with the event train circularly shifted within each song.

hypotheses.body:
## Statement
Conditioning on whole-track structure -- section label and time to the next drop -- is worth more than anything else the offline setting buys, because structure is where the largest measured effect in this project's data lives.

## Rationale
Solberg and Jensenius measured movement at the drop at 1.68x to 2.53x the breakdown level with Cohen's d up to +2.55, and we reproduced that on the Oslo corpus. It is the largest effect anywhere in this project, several times bigger than any frame-level audio-movement correlation, and it is exactly the thing a causal model cannot use: knowing a drop is 8 bars away requires hearing the build finish. A human operator has the setlist and does exactly this.
It is also the honest reason to prefer pre-rendering, as opposed to preferring it because the numbers happen to be higher.

## Plan
Add section label (intro / build / drop / breakdown / core) and signed seconds to the next drop as conditioning channels. Labels come from whole-track Laplacian segmentation plus the EDM role labeller already in lightsem/audio/, validated against the Oslo record's own hand-marked breakdown/buildup/drop times on the two mixes -- the only place in this corpus where the truth is written down. Retrain the offline trunk with and without those channels, everything else identical.

## Statement
Dance is not a category error for light. Light derived from real dance motion through the hybrid conductor (dance envelopes, audio-phased transients), brightness-matched against a 30-line audio beat trigger on the same music, is preferred by a blind rater on at least one of two questions: 'which is on the music?' and 'which looks like a lighting engineer did it?'. ## Rationale
exp-001 showed the hybrid beats the beat trigger on Light-BAS (+0.124 vs +0.094) while staying close to the dance-derived look (FID 43 vs 794). Both arms take transient phase from the same audio beat grid, so 'on the music' is expected to be close; the envelopes and amplitudes the dancer supplies are what the second question can see.

## Plan

## Statement
A fixed anatomical root-local pose chart, rather than fixture-locked lateral lanes, increases emitted broadband motion relative to cone size on the saved Shpongle body while respecting registered group-spread, mechanics and control limits.

## Rationale
Unpreregistered proper-FK engineering already shows raw anatomical inversions retained by prototype, fixed-lane saturation, millimetre pair overlaps and shared 3D-to-2D nullspace. New prediction concerns emitted axes/visibility after mechanics on recordings, not these already-seen synthetic facts. Current source and physical studies still fail musicconditioning; this is a mapper mechanism test, not a music-model fix. It builds on static stage02 and completed optics/lean evidence. Pair convergence is not equivalent to global collapse.

## Statement
A phase-preserving linear codec with explicit root/contact channels can satisfy clean-motion fidelity gates where the 20k nonlinear temporal codec recipe failed.

## Rationale
All original codec arms miss velocity, full-track and physical fidelity. Root-oracle diagnostics show limb velocity errors persist; initial 16s quiet coverage was zero. This revision tests native temporal-detail preservation and separates analytically fitted compression from neural optimization. It is a compound engineering revision, not attribution of failure solely to interpolation or BF16.

## Plan
/mnt/lightsem-data/experiments/lightsem/motion_representation_phasecodec_20260910. One analytic fit to identical full TRAIN records for every rank; equal canonical-song weights, no random training seed or checkpoint selection. Random orthogonal projection initialization is a descriptive control. All four arms evaluated before selection. Music training only after full qualification; no TEST. Frozen original temporal128 is historical baseline, not an exposure-matched optimization comparison.

hypotheses.body:
## Statement
Just Dance coach motion is predictable from audio on held-out songs in a way AIST++ motion was not, because the choreography is made to the song's structure rather than improvised to a structure-less loop: held-out-song R2 for the vertical/energy family reaches +0.20 or more at 2 s and survives partialling out genre and the wiki's Effort rating. If it collapses under genre as AIST++ did, the coach motion is a genre prior and only the background visuals and the structure labels survive from the corpus.

## Rationale
Stage 0b: AIST++ movement is explained by genre (0.65-0.96 of between-track variance) and audio-movement correlations collapse when genre and tempo are partialled out; Oslo free dancing to EDM gives +0.30 on held-out tracks because the music has structure and the dancers respond to it. Just Dance choreography is designed section by section to full commercial songs, so the structure response is built in; but it is one performer per song and the song's genre/difficulty could still explain the between-song variance.

## Plan
rb-ls2-08 step 8.2. Descriptors from the coach through pose2d (masked UI, 30 fps), audio bus (causal and offline) and beat grid on the capture audio, split by song key. hypotheses.body:
## Statement
Most of the gap between the model's light (+0.018 against its null) and light mapped from the real dance (+0.211) is caused by the causality constraint, not by the corpus. The same trunk with unmasked attention over the whole track will close at least half of it.

## Rationale
This is a ceiling measurement and it has to come first, because it decides whether the next month is spent on architecture or on data. Stage 0b already showed the corpus is weak: genre alone explains 0.65-0.96 of between-track movement variance in AIST++, and removing the accidental 375 ms look-ahead cost held-out R2 +0.0438 -> +0.0192, which says look-ahead was worth a lot on this data. If an offline model with the entire track still cannot beat +0.105, then nothing about the model is the binding constraint and the answer is more free-dance-to-EDM data, not a better head.

## Statement
The model's light flashes three times too often because its sampled descriptors carry 11x to 452x the corpus's above-6-Hz energy. Filtering the model's output with the same zero-phase 12 Hz Butterworth the targets were built with will bring the light event rate to the corpus value and lower FID, without costing diversity.

## Rationale
Measured, not guessed: the regressed block sits at 0.3-5x the corpus HF energy and the sampled block at 11-452x, so this is a property of per-frame sampling and not of the trunk. ar_flow was already enabled, so conditioning on the previous output is not sufficient. A causal one-pole was written and is the online fallback, but offline the exact filter the targets were made with is available, and matching the target's own construction is a stronger argument than fitting a time constant.

No retraining. Filter each predicted channel with scipy filtfilt at the corpus's own cutoff, re-render, and re-run the Stage 1 light protocol. ## Statement
The Stage 1 audio bus was not causal, and the Stage 1 light gates were not measuring what the model believes. Removing the look-ahead will cost held-out accuracy, because part of the accuracy was bought with it; calibrating the event threshold to the corpus rate will raise Light-BAS, because the emitted event rate was a constant of the code rather than a decision of the model.

## Statement
Two to four hundred brightness-matched pairwise ratings on held-out songs are enough to fit a Bradley-Terry model over at most 12 conductor knobs, separately for 'fits the music' and 'looks like an engineer did it', with held-out pair accuracy above 60% at n = 200, without pushing Light-BAS toward the metronome, and a fresh batch of raters prefers the fitted knobs to the defaults.

No human preference sits anywhere in the loop; the 10-pair category test showed the two questions dissociate (8-1-1 vs a tie). ## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[audio-predicts-lighting-events-when-the-scene-changes-even-though-it-does-not-pr]].

## Measurements
- [[event-ap-lift-audio-marginal]]: before -0.156836599111557 → after 0.0909034013748169  (Δ +0.24774, up ✓ predicted up)
- [[event-ap-lift-audio-only]]: before 1.1938177347183228 → after 1.2974029779434204  (Δ +0.103585, up)

## Gates
- `beats-circular-shift-null`: PASS — observed marginal lift +0.0909x vs circular-shift null -0.1568 +- 0.0876 over 40 reps -> z +2.83, p 0.000. Required z>2.0 and p<0.05.

**Verdict:** supports

## Notes
POSITIVE -- the first non-null result in this project.

140 songs, 1376 events, 5-fold CV by song, horizon 1.0 s.

  rhythm-only baseline (no audio)   1.3241x lift over base rate
  audio only                        1.2974x
  rhythm + audio                    1.4151x
  audio's MARGINAL lift             +0.0909x

Circular-shift permutation null (40 reps; event count and rhythm preserved,
only audio alignment destroyed):
  marginal null    -0.1568 +- 0.0876  ->  observed z +2.83, p 0.000
  audio-only null  +1.1938 +- 0.0519  ->  z +2.00

GATE MET (preregistered z > 2.0, p < 0.05).

The null mean is NEGATIVE (-0.1568): under shift, adding audio features HURTS
the rhythm baseline via added variance. So the observed positive marginal is
not an artifact of extra parameters -- extra parameters cost you here, and
audio still wins.

WHY THIS WORKED WHERE LEVELS FAILED: on the level target persistence scored
+0.708 and audio's marginal was -0.005. That comparison was structurally
rigged. Moving to events removes the edge, and the SAME audio features that
were worthless become significant. The failure was the target formulation,
not the features and not the model.

CONFOUND, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED (probe_cut_vs_light.py, 36 songs, native 30fps,
968 events): the target derives from stage VIDEO, so a camera cut looks like a
lighting change, and concert video is edited on the music. If cuts dominated,
this would be audio->editing, not audio->lighting.
  median rise time 18 frames = 0.60 s   (a cut is ~1 frame)
  only 13.5% rise in <=2 frames
  only 8.4% revert to the pre-event state within 4.5 s
  57.6% move to a NEW state and stay there
Gradual and persistent = lighting-like, not cut-like. This does NOT prove the
absence of edit contamination -- that needs shot-boundary labels the dataset
does not ship -- but it bounds it as a minority of events.

SCOPE, stated plainly: z=+2.83 establishes the coupling EXISTS. It does not
establish it is large enough to build a rig on (+0.0909x lift is modest), and it
does not say WHICH audio property carries it. That attribution is the next
probe and it is project-defining: if plain ENERGY carries all of it, the
industry's L2 threshold triggers are already at the ceiling and 'semantic'
buys nothing.

## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[light-derived-from-real-dance-motion-by-a-fixed-a3ac3d]].

## Measurements
- [[light-bas-minus-shift-null]]: before 0.0942 → after 0.0082  (Δ -0.086, down ✗ predicted up)
- [[fid-light-kinetic]]: before 1.82 → after 109.66  (Δ +107.84, up ✓ predicted up)
- [[light-diversity-kinetic]]: before 12.342 → after 6.32  (Δ -6.022, down)

## Gates
- `G1`: **FAIL** — oracle Light-BAS / metronome = 0.444 (needed 0.9). The gate is unreachable by design: the metronome reference is 1.0 by construction, so 0.9 x metronome demands metronome behaviour, which section 7 of the plan names as the trap this metric exists to expose. Restated as G1b.
- `G1b`: **FAIL** — conductor v0 (motion only): BAS - own shift null = +0.0082, CI [-0.0101, 0.0259] — includes 0. Audio beat trigger on the same clips: +0.0942, CI [0.0828, 0.1063]. Hybrid (dance envelopes, audio-phased transients): +0.1242, CI [0.1141, 0.1353] — beats both.
- `G2`: PASS — FID_light split-half floor 1.82 (sd 0.37), x3 = 5.45, versus 109.7 against the 1 s block-shuffled null and 922 against the beat trigger. The null was changed from the preregistered circular shift because every delta feature is shift-invariant by construction, so a circular shift would have passed a gate that tests nothing.

**Verdict:** refutes

## Interpretation
**Failure mode:** `mechanism_wrong`

The idea survives, the assumed mechanism does not. The hypothesis assumed a dancing body carries the musics timing into the light. It carries the PERIOD (footfall Rayleigh R 0.55, median z 5.2 per clip) but not the PHASE, which belongs to the choreography and is therefore not in the audio and not learnable from it. Dance supplies WHAT the light does (how much, how wide, which side, how deep the bounce, when the look changes); audio supplies WHEN the transients land. Evidence that this is a fix and not a retreat: the hybrid conductor built on that split scores +0.124 (CI [+0.114,+0.135]) against +0.094 (CI [+0.083,+0.106]) for the audio-only beat trigger, while staying close to the dance-derived look (FID 43 to the oracle vs 794 to the beat trigger). Stage 1 trains block A as regression on dance-derived envelopes and block B as a hazard conditioned on audio beat phase, never an absolute event phase copied from the dancer. Stage 0c must compare the HYBRID against the beat trigger, brightness-matched; comparing the motion-only oracle would test a straw man this experiment already shows is mistimed.

## Notes
Stage 0a built and measured. What it establishes:
(1) The pipeline is real: 1408 clips -> descriptors (30 channels, 3 blocks) -> canonical-rig DMX -> renders, 9 ms per clip; DMX encode/decode round-trips to quantisation error.
(2) FID_light on delta features discriminates (G2 passes by a factor of 20).
(3) Dance-derived light is NOT musically phased on this corpus (G1b fails), and that is a fact about where musical timing lives, not a bug: the dance is period-locked (footfall Rayleigh R = 0.55, median z = 5.2 per clip) with a phase that belongs to the choreography.
(4) The architectural consequence, measured rather than assumed: envelopes and amplitudes come from the dancer, transient PHASE comes from the audio. The hybrid conductor built on that split scores +0.124 (CI [+0.114, +0.135]) against +0.094 (CI [+0.083, +0.106]) for the audio-only beat trigger, while staying close to the dance-derived look (FID 43 to the oracle versus 794 to the beat trigger). This is the same two-path architecture PLAN.md section 4 derives from latency limits — two independent arguments, one design.
Two corpus bugs were found and fixed first, both of which would have silently sunk Stage 1: librosa's beat tracker returned octave-wrong tempi (161.5 BPM for an 80 BPM track) and the phase locked to the off-beat when snare/hat flux exceeded the kick's; the replacement is a constant-tempo comb with a log-normal prior, period from broadband onset and phase from 40-120 Hz kick flux at 5.8 ms resolution, which recovers the corpus's true 80/90/100/110/120/130 BPM design on 58 of 60 tracks. And the first footfall detector fired 2.1 times per beat on planted-foot marker jitter; hysteresis (lift above 0.12 torso lengths, then contact below 0.05) brought it to 0.69 per beat and moved footfall locking from z = 1.4 to z = 5.2.

## Summary

## Measurements
- [[descriptor-audio-r2-over-identity]]: before 0.3 → after 0.192  (Δ -0.108, down ✗ predicted up)

## Gates
- `G-audit`: **FAIL** — No channel comes close. Per-clip audit: audio's held-out R2 is <= 0.15 everywhere and dancer identity wins on 23 of 29 channels (footfall rate identity R2 0.403 vs audio 0.035; vertical bounce amplitude 0.241 vs -0.018). Shared-component audit (across-dancer mean, the only target an audio-only model can reach): best between-track R2 is hand_spread 0.211, CI [-0.075, +0.464], and metric_level 0.150, CI [-0.026, +0.361] — every CI includes zero. Within-track dynamics are small but real: laterality 0.192, CI [+0.064, +0.325]; hand_speed 0.183, CI [-0.004, +0.337]; com_speed 0.128; hip_yaw_speed 0.117; vertical bounce 0.092. The gate asked for > 0.3 on QoM, vertical bounce, head speed and metrical level; all four are below 0.05 within-track.

**Verdict:** refutes

## Interpretation
**Failure mode:** `recipe_conditional`

The recipe is conditional on the corpus. Dance-derived supervision only carries audio information when the music is the only thing that varies; in a choreographed corpus the choreography carries it instead. Practically: (a) keep AIST++ for what it is good for — style priors per genre, motion realism as an FID reference, and validating the video-to-pose path against mocap; (b) get free-dancing data for block A (Oslo EDM club mocap, CC-BY-4.0, 16 and 29 dancers to DJ-mixed EDM with drop/break annotations), which is also the concert domain the product actually ships into; (c) in the meantime train Stage 1 with the honest ceiling in mind — within-track shared dynamics at R2 0.1-0.2, timing from audio, style from a genre token — and never report a block A number without the reliability ceiling next to it.

## Notes
Gate fails and the reason is the corpus, not the method. Three things are now measured rather than assumed:
(1) There IS a large, highly reliable shared movement component in AIST++ (split-half reliability of the across-dancer mean reaches 0.94), so the averaging design works.
(2) That component is genre, not audio: the genre label explains 0.65-0.96 of between-track movement variance, and audio recovers genre only weakly (28 % accuracy over 10 genres from 10 track-mean features, chance 10 %; a proper audio classifier would do better, so this is a floor).
(3) Within a track, causal audio does predict a little of the shared dynamics — laterality R2 0.192 (CI [+0.064, +0.325]), hand speed 0.183, centre-of-mass speed 0.128, hip yaw 0.117, vertical bounce 0.092 — which is the honest ceiling for a dance-supervised block A trained on this corpus.
Two method bugs were found and fixed during the audit, both of which produced spectacular nonsense first: selecting the ridge penalty on data the model had been fitted to (held-out R2 of -19), and scoring audio against a single dancer's trace rather than the across-dancer mean, which charges audio for variance no audio model could explain.

**Verdict:** supports

## Interpretation
Corpus, not concept. Block A is alive: keep the plan's deterministic skeleton, but train and calibrate it on free dancing to concert music rather than on choreographed studio dance. Practical consequences: (a) the movement target is a gain-normalised envelope, never an absolute level; (b) the drop/breakdown contrast is the headline feature for festival lighting and it is worth an explicit structure head; (c) AIST++ keeps a role — style priors per genre, motion realism, and validating the video-to-pose path — but it is not the block A corpus; (d) 20 minutes of Oslo mocap is enough to calibrate and to test, not to train a Conformer, so scaling free-dance data is now the binding constraint on Stage 2.

## Notes
The coupling exists, in the domain the product ships into. Three numbers:
(1) A crowd hearing one mix moves together — split-half reliability of the across-dancer mean is 0.61 to 0.93 (rising with timescale), mean pairwise inter-dancer correlation 0.16 to 0.61. Compare AIST++, where the shared component was equally reliable but turned out to be the genre label.
(2) The drop response is the largest effect measured anywhere in this project: movement at the drop is 1.68x to 2.53x the breakdown level, Cohen's d +1.30 to +2.55, all CIs far from zero, replicating Solberg & Jensenius 2017 on their own data with an independent pipeline.
(3) Causal acoustic features predict the shared movement curve on tracks held out entirely: R2 +0.30 (CI [+0.225,+0.373]) at the 8 s timescale on the 19-dancer mix, against a reliability ceiling of 0.87 correlation. That is two to three times the best AIST++ number and, unlike it, the CI is clear of zero.
One modelling correction on the way: regressing ABSOLUTE movement on ABSOLUTE loudness across contiguous time blocks scored negative R2 everywhere, because each track in a DJ mix sits at its own mix level and the model fails on the offset before it reaches the shape. A real lighting desk has automatic gain; normalising both sides by a causal trailing 30 s window turns the same data from -0.72 to +0.30. Absolute levels were already ruled out on RPMC-L2 in August; this is the same lesson arriving from the other side.

First, the block A / block C boundary was drawn from the literature and should be redrawn from the Stage 0b audit: on this corpus almost nothing clears the identity baseline, so almost everything belongs in the SAMPLED block, not the regressed one. Regressing an unpredictable channel does not produce a cautious estimate, it produces a flat line, and a flat line makes bad light. Second, the flow head samples each frame independently given the trunk state, so its variety is high-frequency jitter rather than the burst-and-rest structure real dance has; it needs to condition on its own previous output. ## Notes
The machinery works and the corpus is the ceiling, as Stage 0b predicted.
What passed: causality is exact (leak 0.0), the model trains in 9 minutes on one RTX 5070, and the generative head does what the literature says it should — the MSE control collapses to 0.000 diversity while the flow head gives 2.03 at the same block A accuracy.
Block A on unseen tracks: mean R2 +0.035, best channels footfall rate 0.220, metrical level 0.082, vertical bounce amplitude 0.038. On unseen DANCERS +0.069. On unseen GENRES -0.183 — negative, meaning worse than predicting the mean, which is exactly what Stage 0b's finding predicts: what the model can learn from this corpus is genre-conditioned style, so removing the genre removes the skill.
Block B events: footfall AP 0.392 against a 0.347 base rate on unseen tracks, 0.655 against 0.572 on unseen dancers; hits show no lift at all. Consistent with Stage 0a — event phase belongs to the choreography.
The light-level gates fail for one identifiable reason rather than three. Predicting near the conditional median makes every channel smooth; a smooth descriptor stream drives a light that flashes constantly and evenly; and an even event train sits at its own circular-shift null however well each flash is phased. The metric is not being unfair — it is naming the failure the plan was built to catch.

Tests hypothesis [[the-august-audio-lighting-event-result-holds-on-da1204]].

## Measurements

**Verdict:** supports

## Interpretation
The operator head is the load-bearing part of the product, and it should be trained first and weighted highest. Dance data explains what a light should DO between cues; operator data explains WHEN to cut, and does so with an effect three times the size. For Stage 3 the conductor should take scene-change timing from the operator head, transient phase from the audio beat grid, and envelopes from the dance-trained head — three sources, each used for what it measurably carries.

## Notes
Confirmed and strengthened at five times the sample size. The August number (+0.09 lift, z +2.83, 140 songs) becomes +0.31 lift (CI [+0.15, +0.48], z 3.66) across 699 shows and 99 held-out songs, with the lag-shift control peaking at zero.
Read it with the same care as before. The shift curve is peaked at 0 but not sharply — neighbouring lags reach 1.46 against 1.48 at zero — which matches the August characterisation of a reactive, timbre-driven coupling over one to two seconds rather than an anticipatory one. Nothing here supports an anticipation claim, and the plan's separate anticipation gate (lift at +4 s above +0.05 with a CI excluding zero) is not tested by this run.
Practical weight: this is the strongest audio-to-light coupling measured anywhere in the project. It comes from professional operators, not from dancers, and it is about WHEN to act rather than what level to hold — the same shape as every other positive result here.

## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[the-deployed-path-meets-its-latency-budget-and-b0aff5]].

## Measurements
- [[audio-to-dmx-latency-ms]]: before 65.0 → after 62.5  (Δ -2.5, down ✓ predicted down)

## Gates
- `G-lat-transient`: PASS — 10.8 ms on its own 5.8 ms hop (a 20 ms budget). Sharing the learned path's 23.2 ms analysis hop costs 28.2 ms and misses, which is the measurement that forces the two paths apart
- `G-lat-learned`: PASS — p50 61.9 ms, p99 62.5 ms, of a 65 ms budget (fixture 30 ms assumed, not measured)
- `G-causal-mech`: PASS — max |dy| over cuts at 50/100/200/300 frames = 0.0

**Verdict:** supports

## Notes
All three software gates pass, and one plan assumption is corrected on the way.
The plan specified a 3-4 s KV cache. That is the attention WINDOW, not the receptive field: windows compose across layers, so six blocks of a 160-frame window plus a 15-tap causal convolution look back 1039 frames, 26 s of audio. The error was not theoretical — chunked inference primed with one window gave block A differences of 0.79 between chunk sizes, meaning the same audio produced different light depending on how it was sliced. With the full context the model costs 3.7 ms p50 and 4.3 ms p99 per frame (against 1.7 ms when under-primed), and the learned path lands at 61.9 ms p50 / 62.5 ms p99 against its 65 ms budget.
The transient path cannot share the learned path's 23.2 ms analysis hop: that alone costs 28.2 ms and misses a 20 ms budget. On its own 5.8 ms hop, onset detection plus network is 10.8 ms. This is an independent, purely engineering argument for the same two-path split that Stage 0a reached from the data.
Not measured here and not claimed: fixture response, Art-Net on a real node, and a photodiode against a click track. The 30 ms fixture term in the budget is an assumption.

## Measurements
- [[event-ap-lift-audio-marginal]]: before 0.3145 → after 0.5553  (Δ +0.2408, up ✓ predicted up)

Build the product around this head. It predicts WHEN to cut, from audio plus the show's own recent rhythm, on professional operator data, with an effect several times anything the dance corpora yield. Also worth carrying forward: on a corpus of this size a linear model on good causal features is a serious competitor, so every neural claim here needs the ridge next to it.

## Notes
HEAD B is deployable and the strongest component measured in this project. The head that gets both the audio and the operator's own recent rhythm predicts the next scene change at 1.805x the base rate against 1.250x for rhythm alone, a margin of +0.555 (CI [+0.385, +0.739]) on 86 held-out shows — nearly double the ridge probe's +0.315 and six times the plan's +0.09 gate.

First, a 3.6 M-parameter Conformer given audio alone (1.347x) does WORSE than a linear ridge on the same 52 features (1.500x); with roughly 500 training shows the capacity is not free, and the gain comes from combining audio with rhythm rather than from depth. Second, an earlier version of this evaluation fitted the rhythm baseline on the test song itself, which inflated it from 1.25 to 2.79 and would have reported the model as far worse than the baseline; the baselines here are fitted on training songs only.

## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[the-stage-1-audio-bus-was-not-causal-and-the-f24efd]].
At commit `master@cab408a+dirty`.

## Measurements
- [[descriptor-audio-r2-over-identity]]: before 0.0438 → after 0.0192  (Δ -0.0246, down ✓ predicted down)
- [[light-bas-minus-shift-null]]: before 0.0212 → after 0.0179  (Δ -0.0033, down ✗ predicted up)
- [[fid-light-kinetic]]: before 69.54 → after 67.29  (Δ -2.25, down ✓ predicted down)
- [[light-diversity-kinetic]]: before 2.572 → after 2.731  (Δ +0.159, up)

## Gates
- `G-feature-causal`: PASS — 23 model-input channels and the 64-band mel bank are bit-identical before the cut when only the future changes; the five beat-grid channels are exempt and the oracle_beat flag is asserted. Before the repair the worst channel was percussive_ratio at 375 ms of look-ahead and a difference of 15x its own standard deviation, from librosa's centred HPSS median; every spectral channel leaked 25 ms from centre=True; onset, pulse_clarity and the mel bank carried a thin whole-clip dependence through top_db.
- `G-rate`: PASS — footfall 0.8867 -> 0.898 ev/s against a corpus 0.896; jump 0.9165 -> 0.024 against 0.026; hit 0.8413 -> 1.352 against 1.353. Fitted on 40 val_track clips, never on training or test clips.
- `G-bas-up`: **FAIL** — REFUTED against the right control. Against v2b the model rose +0.0103 -> +0.0179, but v2b was trained on the leaky bus, so that comparison confounds two changes. Scoring the SAME checkpoint on the SAME features with and without the fitted thresholds isolates it: uncalibrated +0.0212 CI [0.0181, 0.0248], calibrated +0.0179 CI [0.0147, 0.0213]. Calibration LOWERED Light-BAS. It improved FID and diversity (69.54 -> 67.29, 2.57 -> 2.73) and it makes the emitted rate the model's decision rather than the code's, which is why it is kept -- but the predicted mechanism was wrong.

**Verdict:** directional_only

> Direction matched, but a preregistered blocking gate did NOT pass. This does not establish the claim.

## Notes
The leak was worth removing and it was not free.
Held-out block A R2 fell from +0.0438 to +0.0192 once the features stopped reading ahead. That is the honest size of what the look-ahead was buying, and it means every block A number recorded before today was measured on a bus a live system cannot build. The causality gate on the MODEL was passing throughout and never had a chance of catching this: it perturbs the model's input, not the input's own construction.
The rate calibration was predicted to raise Light-BAS and did not. Block-B rates now match the corpus to three decimals, but the rendered light still emits 85.8 events per clip against 85.4 uncalibrated and 30.1 for light mapped from the real dance. The light event count did not move at all, which locates the surplus somewhere the event head cannot reach.
Follow-up measurement, and it is the useful result of the day: the model's channels carry 11x to 452x the above-6-Hz energy of the real ones (section_energy 116x, space_eff 202x, weight 343x, hand_spread 452x), while the REGRESSED block A channels sit at 0.3-5x. The targets are mocap through a 12 Hz Butterworth and are physically smooth; a flow head sampled per frame is not, even with ar_flow already enabled and conditioning on its own previous output. That jitter is what crosses the visibility threshold on the wash fixtures and makes the light flash three times too often.
FID moved 69.54 -> 67.29 against a half-null of 67.45. It is now nominally inside the gate by 0.16, which is not a pass anyone should quote -- the split-half floor is 6.26, so the model is still an order of magnitude from being indistinguishable from dance-derived light.

> Direction matched, but a preregistered blocking gate did NOT pass. This does not establish the claim.

## Notes
The category error did not happen. On 'which looks like a lighting engineer did it' the dance-derived hybrid won 8 of 9 decided trials against the beat trigger on brightness-matched pairs; on 'which is on the music' it was 5-4, a tie, which is what the design predicts because both arms carry the same audio-phased transients.
What the rater's notes add, and this is the useful part: the discriminating cue was dynamics, not timing. T05 (beat trigger): 'too fast changes for light, but on the music actually'. T07 (both bad): 'A does not moving, B is moving boring' -- the hybrid was static on gJS_sBM ch01 and lost both questions. T03 (both bad): equal on both. So the hybrid loses when its envelopes are flat, and the beat trigger loses when it flashes on every beat. That is the same failure exp-009 measured in the model's light (85.8 events per clip against 30.1 real-mapped) seen through a human: a light that changes on every beat is 'on the music' and is not 'a lighting engineer'.

Two readings. (1) The mechanism is confirmed and it is large: matching the sampled channels' spectrum to the corpus takes model light from a chance-level Light-BAS to above the real-mapped value (+0.2106) and FID from the block-shuffle null to a third of it, with diversity across clips not falling. (2) The filter the hypothesis named -- the targets' own 12 Hz zero-phase Butterworth -- does almost nothing, because the mismatch is not at 12 Hz: the corpus channels are smooth well below that and the fitted cutoffs sit near 0.2 Hz. The causal one-pole at those constants already captures the gain, so this is NOT an offline-only win; the offline arm buys the removal of the one-pole's lag (up to 1 s on eight channels) and is scored above. Caveats that go with the number: eight channels hit the 1 s cap, which flattens them; the model's light is now more beat-locked than real-dance light because most of its events come from the audio-phased transient path, and whether that reads as better light is the Stage 3 human question, not a metric one.

**Failure mode:** `recipe_conditional`

The ceiling test did its job in one run: with the entire track visible, symmetric context and the offline bus, held-out block A R2 does not move and the light gates do not move, on AIST++. So the gap between model light and real-mapped light is not a causality tax and not a context-length problem; it is the corpus (Stage 0b: AIST++ movement is explained by genre, not audio). Three architecture experiments would have confirmed this slowly. Consequence: H-C (structure conditioning) is tested on Just Dance, where songs have structure, not on AIST++; and the pre-rendered path's honest advantages are H-B's lag removal and H-C/H-D anticipation, not accuracy.

## Notes
# Optics factorial: scoped observability result, not dancing acceptance

All13 original controls and2 global-brightness matches completed. All15 exact media checks pass:8319frames,30fps,277.3s and identical decoded source-member audio. The later paired movie also passes an independent full decode/count/PCM audit. Original frozen receipts with pending audit fields remain unchanged; separate audit receipts complete the evidence.

## What improved, and against what
The registered active70–90s geometric motion/radius proxy increases **0.140474→0.336552 (2.39583×)** from legacy camera/native zoom/legacy edge to closer camera/zero zoom/angular flux. Camera alone gives **0.113821**, worse on this ratio. This is emitted-axis projection versus a projected half-peak cone radius, NOT decoded optical flow or a music score.

Three independent AI reviews covered all **150 chronological sheets /4170 arm-second samples**, plus **675 native7.5Hz fastframes** in fixed intervals. Sheet thumbnails and attachment downscaling are disclosed. Shafts and endpoints move; fixed source bulbs do not move. The basic six-source fan persists. Angular edges separate the shafts; zero-zoom constant-peak beams can become very dim. Granular shaft texture remains visible. No continuous audiovisual listening or human acceptance occurred.

The brightness-matched comparison retains more separable angular-flux shafts than native-legacy in the inspected samples. Original outside-bulb display-luma means are **3.178096 legacy versus2.936833 flux**. The single legacy RGB scalar **0.924085904** yields **2.963248**, a **+0.026415 (~0.90%) rounding residual** over the target; flux scalar is1. No framewise normalization was used. This controls global mean display brightness, not local contrast, perceived brightness, HDR energy or lumens.

The static80s-angle foil uses2×renderer intensity, and measures **5.620365 versus2.936833** moving-flux mean (~1.914×). It changes color/intensity but holds directions. It does not reproduce the moving controls' sampled direction changes. Both matched arms have zero raw any-channel>=250 outside-bulb pixels; the foil has a tiny nonzero fraction, below registered limits. Do not claim zero clipping everywhere.

## Scope
All registered optics controls and chronological sampled coverage are complete. The proxy and control claims are supported by their respective instruments. Music acceptance is explicitly NOT a result: source motion and direct-audio dynamics were held fixed. Neither wider visibility nor this geometric ratio establishes dancing, realism, preference, hardware capability, or pipeline qualification. Defaults remain unpromoted.

## Notes
# Physical-objective study: not a dancing-pipeline fix

The matched seed0, 30000-update intervention improves measured motion physics but fails qualification. No checkpoint selection, default promotion, TEST, seed1 or hardware output.

## Frozen numerical result
- Generated sliding: matched masked-native **0.927721 m/s**, physical **0.389104 m/s**, reference **0.045977 m/s**. Excess falls **0.881744→0.343127 m/s (61.1%)**, but remains above the **0.20 m/s** absolute limit.
- Physical energy score: correct **0.807600**, donor **0.814330**, shifted **0.809226**. Correct advantages **0.8265%** (95% song CI **[-0.5972,2.3746]%**) and **0.2010%** (**[-0.2420,0.6586]%**) fail the required **5% with positive CI lower bounds**. Matched-native advantages are **2.2554% / 0.7182%**, also below 5%. This is the frozen summary-energy-score instrument, not proof that audio has no influence at all.
- Physical/reference kinetic, travel and contact-coverage ratios: **0.87060 / 0.74986 / 0.94054**. Floor and high-frequency excess gates pass. These do not establish musicality.
- Full/chunk FP32 agreement below **1.67e-6** passes a numerical-consistency test, not a drift-quality test. Short/hold coverage gate checks inclusion/masks and reporting, not successful generation of holds.
- Both initial models match all119 prediction hashes and aggregates. Both final arms share exposure and RNG draws. All numerical cells, short supplements, full12 recordings and six Shpongle draws completed.

## Visual evidence and limits
All13 movies and observer receipts are complete. Four independent AI reviews inspected **531 frozen overviews** (12×21+279) and supplementary native 7.5Hz frames. Full software decode and hashes passed. This was NOT continuous audiovisual listening or human acceptance.

The fixed generated draws often replace reference holds, travel and low poses with compact elbow/knee motifs. Physical is sometimes more restrained, but not uniformly closer to reference or better framed. These are descriptive comparisons; one-to-many choreography need not copy every reference pose. On Shpongle, no reference motion exists. The physical body leaves the fixed oblique view later than masked early in the track, but still crops substantially later. Camera cropping alone does not prove anatomical invalidity.

Shafts and endpoints genuinely move. Stationary source bulbs are not evidence of frozen beams. Yet reference, prior and both new models repeatedly map to a six-shaft fan. No consistent physical-over-masked lighting improvement was established. Direct audio lighting dynamics remain enabled, so shared brightness changes cannot establish learned motion conditioning.

The incumbent is only an uncalibrated 2D body comparator; its matched 3D lighting is unavailable. Shpongle has no source body. The visual comparison is therefore incomplete for incumbent lighting, despite complete scheduled movie/sample coverage. Human music-fit acceptance and pipeline qualification remain unset/false, respectively.

Original failed mapping/rendering remains intact. The post-result support revision masks a legacy 58ms tail gap outside the requested clip; seven maps are adopted byte-for-byte. It does not change models, draws, windows, mapping, optics or numerical results. No missing incumbent lighting was fabricated.

**Instrument versus claim:** fixed matched training and frozen numerical evaluation plus sampled visual diagnostics support a scoped physical improvement and failed qualification of this recipe. They do not establish a functioning music-driven dancing-light pipeline or refute every physical objective.

interpretation.lesson: Surface-space targets remove the persistent central focus caused by elevated inward targets. Articulation bandwidth and a complete changing composition are separate gates; spatial spread alone is not dancing to music. All555 half-second frames inspected. Substantial changing separated motion and floor sweeps replace the always-central knot, but the visible composition still mainly uses the same floor-facing crown/fan. Local visual reconvergence around194-201s remains; the strict4-axis1.5m focus duration understates this perceived interval. Do not declare a complete dancing-light fix from track-average gates or these sampled images. Music fit and human acceptance unmeasured.

## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[the-audio-lighting-event-coupling-is-anticipatory-audio-predicts-an-event-severa]].

## Measurements
- [[event-ap-lift-vs-horizon]]: before -0.09778159856796265 → after 0.0031203031539916992  (Δ +0.100902, up ✓ predicted up)

**Verdict:** supports

## Notes
MIXED -- and the honest reading is REACTIVE, not anticipatory.

  horizon   base    marginal lift        null              z       p
    0.2s   0.023     +0.4824      -0.0190+-0.1346    +3.73   0.000
    0.5s   0.056     +0.2085      -0.0688+-0.0812    +3.41   0.000
    1.0s   0.110     +0.0909      -0.1413+-0.0736    +3.15   0.000
    2.0s   0.217     +0.0561      -0.1231+-0.0532    +3.37   0.000
    4.0s   0.380     +0.0031      -0.0978+-0.0308    +3.27   0.000
    8.0s   0.565     -0.0056      -0.0654+-0.0271    +2.20   0.000

The script's own automated verdict said 'ANTICIPATORY' because z stays above 2
at 4 s and 8 s. THAT VERDICT IS REJECTED. Read the effect size, not the z:

  marginal lift +0.4824 (0.2s) -> +0.0909 (1.0s) -> +0.0031 (4.0s) -> -0.0056 (8.0s)

The effect DECAYS BY ~99% BY 4 s AND GOES NEGATIVE BY 8 s. z stays high only
because the permutation null is itself negative and its spread tightens as the
base rate grows, so 'not as bad as the null' registers as significant even when
the absolute lift is zero. High z with a null effect size is not a usable
anticipation window.

The z-based rule in probe_horizon_sweep.py is therefore WRONG and should gate
on absolute marginal lift instead. Recorded rather than silently patched, since
the flawed rule produced a claim that had to be overturned by hand.

WHAT THIS MEANS: the coupling is real (permutation-validated at every horizon)
but SHORT-RANGE. Audio tells you an event is happening within ~1-2 s, not that
one is coming in 4-8 s. Peak lift is at the SHORTEST horizon tested (0.2 s,
+0.4824x), which is the signature of detection, not prediction.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PRODUCT: the original L3 pitch -- light that LEADS a
build-up -- is NOT supported by this data at the 4-8 s lead times that pitch
implies. What IS supported is smarter DETECTION: reacting to timbral change
rather than loudness, at ~1 s latency. That is a real improvement over
threshold triggers (which key on the feature that this data says does not
work) but it is a weaker claim than anticipation and must not be sold as one.

The anticipation the DSP baseline demonstrated on synthetic EDM (2.78 s lead)
does not transfer here. RPMC-L2 is Rock/Punk/Metal livehouse material, which
lacks the long telegraphed build-ups that make EDM anticipation possible. The
lead-time claim may be genre-specific and remains untested on EDM with real
lighting ground truth.

## Summary
Tests hypothesis [[the-audio-lighting-event-signal-is-carried-by-loudness-energy-if-true-the-indust]].

## Measurements
- [[event-ap-lift-by-feature-family]]: before 1.4381231880187988 → after 1.4704288244247437  (Δ +0.0323056, up ✓ predicted up)

**Verdict:** supports

## Notes
REFUTED, and the refutation is GOOD NEWS for the project.

Energy is the ONLY family that fails to beat its own null. Marginal lift over
the rhythm baseline (1.3241x), 140 songs, horizon 1.0 s:

  family      dim     lift      marg        null            z       p
  energy        2   1.4704   +0.1463   1.4381+-0.0488   +0.66   0.240
  harmonic      2   1.3832   +0.0590   1.4609+-0.0550   -1.41   0.960
  openl3      512   1.4151   +0.0909   1.2794+-0.0539   +2.52   0.000
  spectral     10   1.7060   +0.3818   1.4562+-0.0593   +4.21   0.000
  timbre      128   1.6203   +0.2962   1.3302+-0.0582   +4.98   0.000

THREE FINDINGS:

1. ENERGY IS NOT SIGNIFICANT (z=+0.66, p=0.240). Loudness does NOT
   explain when a lighting operator changes the scene. This directly contradicts
   the assumption behind FFT-threshold rigs. The industry's L2 approach is not
   at the ceiling here -- it is keying on the wrong feature.

2. TIMBRE (MFCC, z=+4.98) AND SPECTRAL (z=+4.21) CARRY THE SIGNAL.
   Operators respond to a change in the CHARACTER of the sound -- distortion
   coming in, a section changing texture -- not to it getting louder. On
   Rock/Punk/Metal livehouse material that is musically sensible: these genres
   are loud throughout, so loudness is uninformative while timbre is not.
   This is the specific, defensible claim that an L3 semantic model has
   headroom, and it NAMES the features that model must encode.

3. openl3 (z=+2.52) is BEATEN by 10 hand-picked spectral descriptors
   (z=+4.21) despite having 512 dimensions. The learned general-purpose
   embedding is not the right representation for this task. A bespoke encoder
   over spectral/timbral descriptors is better motivated than fine-tuning
   openl3 -- and it is far cheaper.

CAVEAT: 'timbre' here is MFCC. RPMC-L2 ships no zero-crossing-rate despite an
earlier schema note claiming it, so no separate percussive family was testable.
MFCC and the spectral descriptors are correlated; this probe establishes that
NON-ENERGY spectral character carries the signal, not which of the two is
primary.
